ai_summary: Great Britain is currently recording a total wind output of 8.8 GW, with Scottish wind generation contributing an estimated 3.3 GW, which corresponds to 32.7% of Scotland’s installed wind capacity. This robust renewable generation has driven Scottish carbon intensity down to an exceptional 0 gCO2/kWh, standing in stark contrast to the GB-wide carbon intensity of 74 gCO2/kWh. However, transmission bottlenecks between Scotland and demand centres further south continue to constrain power flows. So far today, 9,491 MWh of Scottish generation has been curtailed through Balancing Mechanism bids at a direct constraint cost of about £245,788. To compensate for this stranded green energy, an estimated 1,803,252 m3 of natural gas had to be burned elsewhere on the grid, adding 3,322 tonnes of CO2 to the atmosphere. Extrapolated over a full year, the total yearly cost of curtailment reaches approximately £90 million, which increases electricity invoices by an estimated £0.30/MWh for consumers across the UK. These figures underscore the urgent economic and environmental case for upgrading cross-border transmission infrastructure to stop wasting zero-carbon generation and reduce consumer costs.
